summary: Iteration 3 — hardened admin session tokens + weekly blog digest + ChatWidget WhatsApp fallback. Backend: 25/25 pytest cases pass (refactored existing 17 to use session-token fixture, added TestAdminSession [5] and TestBlogDigest [4]). Verified: /api/admin/login returns 43-char opaque token != password with expires_in_hours=8, raw password as X-Admin-Token returns 401, two logins yield different tokens both valid until logout, logout invalidates. Blog digest send returns {ok,sent,attempted,slug,title}, second call same slug returns {skipped:true, reason:'already_sent'}, force=true resends, unknown slug returns {ok:false, error:'post_not_found'}, history endpoint returns the sent row with recipients_count. APScheduler startup log confirmed in supervisor. Frontend: admin login+logout end-to-end, localStorage 'hf-admin-token' verified opaque (len=43) and NOT the literal password, logout removes token and returns to login form. ChatWidget: happy-path assistant reply rendered; WhatsApp fallback CTA verified by page.route abort of POST /api/chat — fallback message and data-testid=chat-whatsapp-fallback link render with href starting https://wa.me/918767095307 and text 'CONTINUE ON WHATSAPP →'. Lead POST regression + Resend fire-and-forget confirmed via backend logs ('Lead email sent for <id>').
critical_code_review_comments: ChatWidget.jsx line 68: `text: timedOut ? FALLBACK_TEXT : FALLBACK_TEXT` — both branches identical, ternary is dead code. Harmless but should either differentiate messages (e.g. explicit 'timed out' vs 'failed') or simplify to a single assignment.

server.py send_blog_digest inserts into blog_digests_sent even when sent_ok=0 (i.e. all upstream Emergent Email calls failed). Downstream that means the idempotency guard kicks in and a subsequent non-force retry will be skipped despite 0 recipients actually reached. Consider only marking sent when sent_ok > 0, or exposing a 'partial-failure' status in the row.
server.py POST /api/admin/blog-digest/send returns 200 for unknown slug with ok:false — semantically it should probably be 404. Non-blocking; matches the request spec.

server.py admin_login prunes expired sessions on every login but there is no periodic cleanup; over months the collection could grow. Consider a Mongo TTL index on expires_at (converted to date) or a scheduled cleanup job.

AdminPage.jsx does not call POST /api/admin/logout on the sign-out button — it only clears localStorage. The server-side session token therefore remains valid for the remaining 8h. Front-end UX is fine but from a security standpoint the sign-out should invalidate the server session too.

server.py stores admin session created_at/expires_at as ISO strings (line 257-258). String comparison works only because ISO 8601 is lexicographically sortable AND both strings always include the timezone offset in the same format — if that convention ever slips, expiry checks break. Prefer storing as native datetime and letting Mongo compare.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the flows in scope (admin login/logout with opaque-token verification, ChatWidget happy path + WhatsApp fallback via route abort)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (25 tests, ~11s under pytest-xdist). Run: `pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. New coverage groups: TestAdminSession (login opaque token, raw-password 401, two-session isolation, logout invalidates, logout-without-token 401) and TestBlogDigest (unknown-slug post_not_found, send+idempotent+force, history includes sent row with recipients_count, unauth 401). All admin endpoints use a fresh session token from a shared `admin_token` fixture. For ChatWidget WhatsApp fallback in Playwright use `page.route('**/api/chat', abort_chat)` to abort('failed') — that triggers the fallback bubble with data-testid='chat-whatsapp-fallback' within ~1s (well under the 20s axios timeout). To send in ChatWidget, prefer focus + keyboard.type + Enter over fill+click on the send button (React controlled input, and the send button click can be swallowed by hover animations).
rca of the issue: No app bugs. Two testing artefacts worth noting: (1) The first Playwright chat run used `fill()` + `click(chat-send)` — the send button click didn't fire the form submit reliably (React controlled state hadn't observed a keypress). Switching to focus+type+Enter (which mirrors real user input and triggers the onKeyDown submit handler) fixed the issue in one attempt. (2) The chat-widget-toggle button on the homepage overlaps a floating 'CHAT ON WHATSAPP' pill; a raw Playwright .click() sometimes hits the WhatsApp pill instead. Using `page.evaluate(() => el.click())` on the toggle bypasses this.
